ops.title: No gate catches a doc naming a symbol the census deleted
ops.description:
Found 2026-08-01: docs/DESIGN.md documented `Staged()` in six places for the whole span between the
rename landing and someone noticing, and release-check.sh --tree, export-census.sh, gen-package-table.sh
--check and check-codegen.sh all passed the entire time. DESIGN is normative — scripts/mixed-era.sh
cites §8.4 — so a stale normative doc is worse than a stale README.

The proposed gate, from the lane that fixed it: docs name exported symbols in backticks, and
ci/exported.txt is already the machine-checked census. Two shapes —

(a) extract backticked identifier tokens from docs/*.md and require membership in the census;
(b) cheaper and more precise: have export-census.sh's deleted/renamed ledger grep docs/**.md and fail
    on any hit, which flags the symbol in the same commit the rename lands.

(b) is preferred: it fires exactly when the damage is done, and it cannot produce the false positives
(a) would on prose that mentions a Go stdlib name or a consumer's symbol.

What NO mechanical gate catches, and which stays with review: behavioural drift that names no dead
symbol. All three of these were live in DESIGN alongside the dead `Staged()` and none would trip
either shape — "digest-keyed" for a path that is now Label-keyed, "copies at construction" for a
constructor that no longer writes, and ValidateForServe described as durations-only when it carries
the Label rule.

ops.text: A doc naming an exported symbol absent from ci/exported.txt fails a gate in the same commit the rename lands
